Dutiyaesanāsutta Searches (2nd)

Vuttañhetaṁ bhagavatā vuttamarahatāti me sutaṁ: This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.

“Tisso imā, bhikkhave, esanā. “Mendicants, there are these three searches. Katamā tisso? What three? Kāmesanā, bhavesanā, brahmacariyesanā—The search for sensual pleasures, the search for continued existence, and the search for a spiritual path. imā kho, bhikkhave, tisso esanā”ti. These are the three searches.”

Etamatthaṁ bhagavā avoca. The Buddha spoke this matter. Tatthetaṁ iti vuccati: On this it is said:

“Kāmesanā bhavesanā, “The search for sensual pleasures, for continued existence, brahmacariyesanā saha; and the search for a spiritual path; Iti saccaparāmāso, the holding tight to the thought, ‘this is the truth’, diṭṭhiṭṭhānā samussayā. and the mass of grounds for views—

Sabbarāgavirattassa, for one detached from all lusts, taṇhakkhayavimuttino; freed by the ending of craving, Esanā paṭinissaṭṭhā, that searching has been relinquished, diṭṭhiṭṭhānā samūhatā; and those grounds for views eradicated. Esanānaṁ khayā bhikkhu, With the ending of searches, a mendicant nirāso akathaṅkathī”ti. is free of hope and indecision.”

Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti. This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.

Chaṭṭhaṁ.
